head.citation-title: Study on the influence of concrete core filling on the dynamic response and crack resistance of offshore prestressed pipe piles during hammering piling
head.abstracts: © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.To address the engineering problem of cracking in offshore prestressed concrete pipe piles during hammer piling, this study conducted field pile driving tests on conventional open-ended pipe piles and novel double-ended core-filled pipe piles at a wharf project. Using field-measured data and ultrasonic damage detection after pile installation, the dynamic response of core-filled piles and the mechanisms by which core filling improves strain distribution and crack resistance were examined. Test results show that the novel core-filled piles exhibit higher stiffness and greater energy dissipation capacity, effectively improving their dynamic stress state. Compared with conventional piles, the maximum longitudinal compressive and tensile strains of the pile body were reduced by 29% and 64%, respectively, the transverse tensile strain reached only 46% of the concrete cracking threshold, and the duration of stress wave oscillation was shortened. Ultrasonic testing further revealed only a 6% maximum attenuation in wave velocity and a peak damage variable of 0.134, confirming enhanced crack resistance. In addition, a dynamic analysis model for pile driving was developed based on the stroke characteristics of diesel hammers, effectively quantifying the energy contribution of each hammer stroke to the pile penetration depth. This study provides both an experimental basis and theoretical guidance for the structural optimization, construction quality control, and hammering parameter optimization of offshore prestressed concrete pipe piles.
